subject: Brownfield SIEM Connector — Acceptance & Staging Validation
messages:
From: Tom Reed <tom.reed@globex.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-04-12T09:12:00Z
Subject: SIEM connector validation plan for brownfield VPC

Evelyn,

Thanks for taking this on. We're preparing the brownfield rollout for our on-prem instances and we'd like to validate the SIEM connector behavior before we flip the forwarding in production. High level ask: acceptance testing in our staging VPC that mirrors the brownfield network (NAT + limited egress), plus a short parsing/field-mapping validation for our Splunk instance.

Can Redwood validate:
- that logs forwarded from the forwarder reach our Splunk HEC endpoint over mTLS
- that the event timestamps and host fields survive your enrichment layer
- that trace IDs are preserved in the span/trace hooks for X-Ray-compatible traces

We can provide a staging endpoint and a sample log tarball. Proposed window: week of Apr 18.

Attached: sample_logs.tar.gz (3k events subset)

Regards,
Tom Reed
Senior Security Engineer, Globex
[Attachment: sample_logs.tar.gz (application/gzip)]

-----
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Reed <tom.reed@globex.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-04-13T10:05:00Z
Subject: Re: SIEM connector validation plan for brownfield VPC

Tom — thanks, this is clear and doable.

Quick replies to your asks:
- mTLS to Splunk HEC: we support HEC over mTLS in private deployments; we'll need your cert bundle and the endpoint host name.
- enrichment: we can run a short acceptance run with identical enrichment rules to confirm host/timestamp preservation.
- trace propagation: we can enable the tracing hooks and run an end-to-end request that includes Redwood trace headers to confirm X-Trace passthrough.

I've attached a concise test plan and checklist (siem_connector_testplan.xlsx).
Proposed schedule: staging validation on Apr 19 (canary window 4 hours), then a short parsing validation the morning of Apr 20. If that works for you, I'll schedule Redwood infra and loop in Kim + Marissa for the runbook and parsing checks.

Next steps: 1) Share Splunk HEC URL + cert; 2) Confirm access window; 3) We'll publish a short checklist and preflight steps.

Thanks,
Evelyn Hart
Head of Customer Ops, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: siem_connector_testplan.xlsx (application/vnd.ms-excel)]

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>, Tom Reed <tom.reed@globex.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-04-14T08:40:00Z
Subject: Re: SIEM connector validation plan for brownfield VPC

Adding a short technical checklist from the infra side. Tom — a couple of items we'll need verified before the canary: 
- Are outbound ports 443 and 9200 (if using HEC on 9200) allowed from the forwarder subnet? If there is an egress proxy in front of HEC, we need the proxy CA.
- TLS cipher constraints: do you require >TLS1.2 and ECDHE-only? We can configure the forwarder to match.
- NAT session timeouts: our keepalive behavior opens streams that could be reset in networks with aggressive NAT timeouts; confirm your staging NAT idle.
- Tracing hooks: to preserve trace IDs we add X-Redwood-Trace header at the forwarder; please confirm that your Splunk extractor won't strip non-HTTP headers if you route HEC via a proxy.

I'll be running the canary from our dedicated test pool; Marissa will own parsing/field mapping validation.

- Kim
Principal Engineer, Private Deployments

-----
From: Tom Reed <tom.reed@globex.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-04-15T15:22:00Z
Subject: Re: SIEM connector validation plan for brownfield VPC

Kim, Evelyn — thanks. Quick answers:
- Ports: we allow 443 outbound; our HEC listens on 443 in staging (we front it with a TLS terminator).
- Cipher policy: TLS1.2+ required; ECDHE preferred.
- NAT: staging uses a 10 minute NAT idle.
- Proxy: there is an egress proxy with CA we can share; forwarding won't strip headers but some older proxies normalize header keys.

I've uploaded the staging HEC endpoint and cert bundle to the shared Drive: https://drive.globex.com/staging/hec/abcd. Username: globex-siem-staging; note we'll open a short window for your ip ranges on Apr 19 14:00-18:00 UTC.

I'll also attach the subset of logs I sent initially (sample_logs.tar.gz) and a short parsing example that shows our expected Splunk fields (parsing-diff-snippets.txt).

Tom
[Attachment: parsing-diff-snippets.txt (text/plain)]
[Attachment: sample_logs.tar.gz (application/gzip)]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Tom Reed <tom.reed@globex.com>
Date: 2028-04-18T11:03:00Z
Subject: Re: SIEM connector validation plan for brownfield VPC — preliminary parsing results

Team — ran the parsing exercise in our staging mirror this morning during a short preflight. Summary: 
- Ingest: all test events reached the Splunk HEC staging endpoint over mTLS and showed up within ~4s. Good.
- Timestamps: 99.7% preserved. A small subset (~3 events) showed shifted timestamps due to an input timezone marker—I've noted examples in parsing-diff-snippets.txt.
- Host field: host enrichment preserved, but some hostnames were truncated by a Splunk field size limit on the staging index (we flagged the index config).
- Trace propagation: Redwood tracing hook inserted X-Redwood-Trace; header was visible at the HEC terminator. However, one of the proxy hops normalizes header case and our extractor rule is case-sensitive — will need a small extractor tweak on Globex's side or we can add header mapping on our forwarder.

Attachments: parsing-diff-snippets.txt (examples), brief test log summary.

Next steps I recommend before full canary on Apr 19 14:00 UTC: 
1) Globex to share egress proxy CA and confirm extractor case-insensitivity plan (or we add mapping).
2) We'll publish a 30-minute runbook for the Apr 19 window (preflight checks, fallback procedure, rollback trigger).
3) If you want, we can run an optional tracing-only pass to validate spans end-to-end without full event volume.

Marissa Cole
Sr. Product Ops Engineer, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: parsing-diff-snippets.txt (text/plain)]

Tom — thanks for the quick turnaround and for opening the Apr 19 window. We will proceed with the canary at 14:00 UTC as agreed. Final checklist: 
- Globex: confirm egress proxy CA uploaded to Drive and extractor case-insensitivity approach (or give permission for Redwood to add header mapping).
- Redwood: we will push a lightweight forwarder configuration with header mapping enabled as a fallback and hold volume at 1% of normal.
- Marissa: will run the parsing validation and post results within 60 minutes of the window start.
- Kim: infra will monitor NAT session resets and keep a rollback trigger if retransmit rates exceed threshold.

If all of the above is green we'll proceed with a phased ramp to 10% after the first 2 hours. If anything looks off we'll rollback and open a short postmortem.

Thanks everyone — see you in the runbook channel at 13:30 UTC for preflight.

Evelyn Hart
